text.tspan: A deployable command-line application that validates, renders, and
manages Aurora models. The CLI is optimized for deterministic,
automatable workflows (local scripting and CI), and delegates model
semantics (parsing, invariants, rendering) to the shared library.
A deployable application that provides an interactive experience for
creating, editing, and navigating Aurora models. The Editor focuses on
discoverability and safe, incremental iteration with immediate
A VS Code extension that enables authoring, validation, and
visualization of Aurora models within the editor. It provides
trust-aware workspace integration, webview-based UI experiences, and
(optionally) an MCP server surface for other in-editor tooling.
Aurora model source files (cards and schema references) that represent
Generated Markdown and view artifacts produced from Aurora models
(e.g., rendered card pages and view markdown).
The user’s workspace files and settings (including source code and
secrets) that tooling must not corrupt or exfiltrate.
Shared library component used across tooling surfaces to load, validate,
update, and save Aurora models. It is the implementation home for common
parsing, invariants, deterministic rendering, and safe write semantics.
The Tauri/Svelte front-end UI component for the Editor application.
The Rust backend component for the Editor application, hosting the
Editor UI component that presents an explorer tree over the Aurora
Editor UI component that provides a mind-map-like visualization
Editor UI component for editing cards, attributes, and links in an
Editor UI component for viewing and editing human-readable Markdown
Model Context Protocol (MCP) server component used by the VSCode
extension to expose Aurora model operations via the shared library.
Core Aurora domain component providing the aggregate root for working
Aurora model domain component representing a directed graph of cards and
Aurora card domain component representing a single architectural
element with links and audit trail.
Command-line interface component that orchestrates validation, view
rendering, and compact export for Aurora models.
Extension host component responsible for activation, command
registration, workspace integration, and coordinating model operations
Webview UI component hosting interactive model browsing, editing,
visualization, and preview experiences within VSCode.
Component that mediates workspace file operations (open, watch, and
save) with safe defaults and trust-aware behaviors.
Gate potentially unsafe operations (e.g., file writes, webview
rendering, executing tools) behind workspace trust checks and explicit
Safe Path Handling and Atomic Writes
Constrain paths to the intended workspace/model roots, normalize and
validate paths, and use atomic write patterns to prevent partial writes
Sanitize rendered Markdown and webview content, restrict resource
loading, and disable script execution to prevent injection.
Minimize read/write permissions and scope operations to explicit
user-selected paths; avoid reading or writing unrelated workspace files.
A local development deployment where Aurora tooling is built and run
A user workstation environment where the Editor, CLI, and VSCode
Local file system (workspace) used as the primary persistence
mechanism for Aurora model files and generated outputs.
VSCode extension storage for persisted settings and
non-source-of-truth state (cache, UI state, last-opened model, etc.).
Command-line interface surface exposing Aurora model operations as
Model Context Protocol interface surface exposing Aurora operations to

Message-based interface between VSCode extension host and webview UI for

VSCode command surface for invoking Aurora tooling actions (validate,

Tooling could overwrite or corrupt files outside the intended model

Operating in an untrusted workspace could allow unsafe operations that
